concept.title: Pseudo-elements
concept.shortdesc: A pseudo-element starts with :: and selects a part of an element or a piece of generated content. It follows the element selector.

conbody.p: The selector reference lists every pseudo-element that CSSMedia accepts.

section.title: Text parts
section.p: ::first-line selects the first formatted line of a block. ::first-letter selects its first letter, together with the punctuation around it. ::first-letter::prefix and ::first-letter::suffix select that punctuation.

section.title: Generated content, markers and footnotes
section.p: ::before and ::after are positions before and after the content of an element. They exist only when the content property gives them something to show.
::marker selects the marker of a list item. ::before::marker and ::after::marker select the marker of generated content that is a list item.
::footnote-call and ::footnote-marker select the reference that replaces a footnote in the text and the marker at the start of the footnote.
To copy the text of an element into a page margin box, use string-set. See Named strings.

section.title: Pseudo-elements without a target in a PDF
section.p: Some pseudo-elements select ranges or widgets that exist only on screen. ::selection, ::search-text, ::target-text, ::spelling-error, ::grammar-error and ::highlight() select highlighted text. ::placeholder, ::file-selector-button, ::details-content and ::backdrop select parts of form controls and interactive elements. CSSMedia accepts them, but an XML document has nothing for them to select.
